utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's start. Could you call the case please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-03-68, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning to you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution, also good morning to my learned friends from the Defence. I'm here together with co-counsel, Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones, I appear for Mr. Oric. With us are our legal assistant, Ms. Jasmina Cosic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts -- I do apologise, Ms. Adisa Mehic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. She seems to like the other name better because she was smiling. So Mr. Jones, I will -- and Madam Vidovic, I will be meeting the head of all other -- 12.30 in my office, in my Chamber, and we'll report back to you on outcome of the talks after we resume. Any preliminaries? Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Regarding the 65 ter transcript, I would like to submit the position of the Office of the Prosecutor. It is a general principle that it should be that 65 ter transcripts should be confidential. Given, however, the exceptional circumstances of this case, in particular the initiative by this Trial Chamber and the functioning of cutting down the witness list, that consideration -- the Prosecution believes that lifting the seal will not undermine in principle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So the 65 ter transcript will remain in the records, however, in an unsealed form. In other words, it will be publicly filed. All right. Next witness, Izet Redzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Redzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that you are receiving interpretation. And if at any moment you're not receiving interpretation in your language or the volume of the interpretation is high -- too high or too low, please draw our attention and we'll rectify the problem straight away. You are about to start giving evidence as one of the first witnesses of the Defence. You know that you are testifying in the case instituted against Naser Oric. According to our Rules, before you start giving evidence you are required to enter a solemn declaration, to make a solemn declaration, to the effect that in the course of your testimony you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth; it's equivalent to an oath that you would take in many national jurisdictions, sometimes swearing on the Bible, sometimes swearing on the Koran, sometimes on other things. So the usher, who's standing next to you, is going to hand you the text of the solemn declaration. I kindly ask you to read it out loud and that will be your testimony -- your solemn declaration, your solemn undertaking, with this Tribunal that you will be testifying the truth. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down. What's going to happen now, you're going to be asked a series of questions by Madam Vidovic, who is lead counsel for Naser Oric in this case. When she's finished, then -- who will be taking -- Madam Joanne Richardson on the Prosecution side will cross-examine you. You have an obligation in terms of the solemn declaration that you have just made to answer all questions irrespective of who is putting these questions to you. In other words, irrespective of whether they are coming from the Prosecution or from the Defence, you have an obligation to answer them truthfully and as fully and to the best of your knowledge as possible. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, by your leave, may I sit while examining the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Redzic.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, by your leave I will lead in the first part of my examination as regards the witness's personal details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, in view of the fact that we speak the same language, when I complete my question please make a brief pause in order to give the interpreters time to interpret the question and then start your answer so that the Chamber can understand what we are saying and that it can enter the record. Do you understand we?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, will you please tell us your full name?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Izet Redzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You're a Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were born on the 19th of January, 1955, in the village of Dzemat, Vlasenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your father's name is Mustafa and your mother's name is Hanka?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You completed the primary school and the secondary school for mechanical engineering in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From 1978 to 1982 you studied mechanical engineering in Subotica in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You graduated from mechanical engineering in 1982?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You did your military service in 1974 in Ljubljana and in 1975 in Ljubljana and Pula?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This was the technical services and you were a mechanic for weaponry. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your first job was in Sarajevo in 1974 and you worked in UnionInvest as a locksmith?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You left that job in 1978 and then went to study in Subotica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After this in 1982 you returned to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You then got a job in the bauxite mine in Vlasenica and you were manager of machine maintenance. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You remained at this job until the multi-party elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1990?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: From 1986 until 1990 before the multi-party elections, you were a deputy in the Assembly of Vlasenica municipality, an assemblyman that is, for the associated labour council?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the multi-party elections, by a decision of the parliament, you were appointed president of the Executive Board of the Vlasenica Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After the war in 1996 you started to work in the Ministry of Transport and Communications of the Tuzla Podrinje canton?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2004 you testified before this Tribunal for the OTP in another case regarding certain facts, facts I will ask you about today. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Which was the other case, please, Madam? I mean, we need it for the record. I know, but we need it for the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this the Prosecutor versus Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Redzic. Mr. Redzic, it is clear from your personal details that you grew up in north-eastern Bosnia. Is this the Tuzla region?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this area?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war, did this area have its own regional organisation?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was called a subregion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now please show the witness a map. So that the Chamber may follow what the witness is saying, we will use maps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this an excerpt from the road map of the former SFRY, and the scale is 1:500.000. The map is already on the ELMO. Mr. Redzic, please indicate to the Chamber on the map before you, which we can see on our computer screens, which municipalities were comprised in the area you have just called a subregion?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you find Zvornik on the map?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, I believe you have a pen before you. Could you please circle Zvornik with it.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please show the others?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Srebrenica, Vlasenica, and Sekovici. That's five municipalities comprising the Zvornik subregion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Redzic. And where was the seat?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The seat of the subregion was in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there some joint bodies or institutions there?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were some government bodies such as the state security service and the state auditing service. As for political organisations, there was the League of Communists and the Socialist League.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will ask you again to leave some time before my question and your response.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may this map be marked as a Defence exhibit, but I would like it to remain with the witness for a while longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's give it a number, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be D705, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, before the map is removed, could you please initial a corner of the map.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the map to be left with Mr. Redzic for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, were you aware of the ethnic composition of the municipality -- of the municipalities before the war?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Chamber the ethnic composition of the population of north-eastern Bosnia according to the census of 1991, bearing in mind the municipalities you circled on the map?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Let's take them in turn. As for Zvornik municipality it had 499 square metres; 81.111 inhabitants. According to the census of 1991, 59.5 per cent were Muslims; 38 per cent were Serbs; and the remainder were others, Yugoslavs and undeclared. As for Bratunac municipality it had 293 square kilometres; 33.575 inhabitants; 64.4 per cent were Muslims; and 34.3 were Serbs. The remainder were Yugoslavs and neutral. Srebrenica municipality had 5 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the number of square kilometres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 73 per cent of the population were Muslims; 25 per cent were Serbs; and the remainder were Yugoslavs or unaffiliated. As for Vlasenica municipality, it had 507 square kilometres; 33.817 inhabitants; 55.2 per cent were Muslims; 42.6 per cent were Serbs; and the rest were others. As for Sekovici municipality, it had 9.639 inhabitants; 184 square kilometres. Of the total number of inhabitants I mentioned, 3.5 per cent were Muslims, 95 per cent were Serbs, and the rest were Yugoslavs or unaffiliated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Redzic. When you were giving this information you had in mind the situation according to the census of 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because you were speaking in the present tense, so we wish to clarify this situation for the record. Very well. Thank you. How did you arrive at this information? How do you know this information?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: As the president of the executive council, my role in 1991 was to monitor this and to establish a commission of which I was the head and to monitor the census and also the census of -- not only of the population but also of all other goods and assets. And I was to execute the decision of the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina of 1991 regarding the census.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, after the census, did you analyse the results of the census and arrive at the data you have supplied?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was my role and task because not only in the subregion but all over Bosnia and Herzegovina I had to know all these details because when we were dealing with economic social welfare or any other needs, we had to have this data at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Looking at the ethnic composition of the population, which part of the population dominated in the Podrinje area?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Of the total number of inhabitants, 63 point something per cent were Muslims in the subregion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What were the inter-ethnic relations like until just before the outbreak of the war in Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Exceptionally good and friendly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, following the Chamber's instructions, I will not ask you many questions about the breakup of Yugoslavia and the political events in Bosnia and Herzegovina before the war. I will put only those questions that are closely connected to our case. So although we discussed many other matters, I will put only specific questions to you now. Please tell Their Honours what, in your opinion, had the greatest impact on the changes in the climate, the atmosphere in Podrinje, starting in 1989, if there were such changes at all?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course there were changes. And the most important cause was the flood of misinformation and untruths on the radio, television, and the media, the infiltration of people from various republics who spread hatred. The Serbs were told they were under threat. The Serb people were intimidated, regardless of whether truths or falsehoods were used to achieve that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Apart from this media activity, was there any influence by government bodies outside Bosnia and Herzegovina as regards propaganda?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a report of the SDB of Serbia in mid-1989. The state security services of Serbia issued some documents to show that Serbs were moving out of Serbia and Bratunac in large numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to show the witness exhibit Defence number 635.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the republican SUP of Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, SDB, 7520; the date is 21st of September, 1989.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to say that in this document you may notice that certain things have been underlined. I would like to say that the Defence has obtained this document in this particular way, that the Defence has not underlined anything in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, could you please look at the first part of this document which reads -- I can see that you are looking at it already. I am going to read it to you. "The Presidency of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the council for the protection of constitutional order of Bosnia and Herzegovina at their sessions held on the 20th of September, 1989, were informed by the republican SUP of the SDB of Serbia, dated 24 August, 1989, that they received from a member of the Presidency of the SFRY from Bosnia-Herzegovina Mr. Bogic Bogicevic, that was given to him by Mr. Borisav Jovic, the vice-president of the Presidency of Yugoslavia." Now, look at the third paragraph, and I quote: "In view of the information and such claims, as well as the fact that the SDB of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina has not received the cited report from the SDB of the SR Serbia (which would be in accordance with the work of the SDB rules and the already good cooperation between the neighbouring SDB centres) and has not obtained this information through its own work, nor have the statements from your reports. Strictly confidential number..." is quoted here, "have been confirmed by your intelligence work of which we informed you in our official document ..." and the number is mentioned here, the date "24 July, 1989." You see the date here, don't you? "We hereby request from the SDB of the Socialist Republic of Serbia to urgently send the report to us, and the documents, based on the dates on which it was compiled in order to fully inform the competent organs and take the necessary measures in our competence." Mr. Redzic, with this regard let me ask you this: You have just told us that you were a member of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica during the period that comprised also the year 1989. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During that period of time and in that capacity, did you receive information that concerned political developments in the north-eastern part of Bosnia in the region that is known as the subregion of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. We as a parliamentary body received all this information for the entire Bosnia; the subregion was the priority of those five municipalities. At our meetings under the item "security situation in the subregion and in the municipalities," we obtained this information that was forwarded to us from the SDB of Serbia. Later on we were informed because the police from the SDB informed the Assembly that the information was not correct and that whatever one could read in newspapers and see on TV was completely incorrect, and the goal of all that was completely different.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You have told us that you resided and you -- that you worked in that area. Did you have any information as to whether the Serb population was moving out under the pressure of Muslims in that area?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. There may have been some movement because of the earthworks in that area; however, there was no emigration [Realtime transcript read in error "immigration"] under the pressure of Muslims. That is absolutely incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber how come that this information and the propaganda that you have just spoken about had any influence on the Serbian population of Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The influence was good because the Serbs believed all this information. They did not go into the essence of this information. From that information onwards, all of a sudden the Serbs started separating themselves from the rest of the population and they started getting closer to Serbia and its leadership.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Redzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: I have a question just to clarify the transcript. The Defence was asking: "Did you have any information as to whether the Serb population was moving out under pressure of the Muslims in that area?" And the answer was: "Absolutely not there was some movement because of some earth works in that area in other words, there was no immigration under the pressure of Muslims." I think that should read "emigration"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Emigration, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes. You don't need to have an answer from -- it's definitely emigration and not immigration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: With regard to this, Mr. Redzic, let me ask you this: Were people moving from one municipality to another for economic reasons?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was precisely the case. I have just said that people moved from Srebrenica to Vlasenica for economic reasons because of the exploitation of bauxite. In Srebrenica there were Serbs with their property, and that was the only method, the only way, how a small percentage of Serbs moved from Srebrenica to the territory of Vlasenica, and that was the long and the short of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Redzic. I'm now going to move to another topic. At the sessions of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica during the year 1988 and 1989, did you discuss any issues that had to do with the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the cause of these discussions?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: We received a written order from the republican institutions that all the municipalities in the ex-Yugoslavia had to issue their municipal decisions on the Territorial Defence and its equipment and their accommodation and billeting in the barracks. This was a document of the Main Staff of the Army of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to the weapons and the other equipment of the Territorial Defence, is there anything specific about the ownership of all that?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely yes. According to the concept of the Territorial Defence, the Territorial Defence and all its assets were purchased by the local population, i.e., the companies and socio-political organisations in the area, and this weaponry could only be used by that particular socio-political organisation in case of a natural disaster or some other hardships. So the weapons and the equipment that belonged to the Territorial Defence were not purchased by the army but by the local population.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to the then-prevailing laws, who was in charge of all the weapons that belonged to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was the civilian authorities. That was the whole underlying cause of this. The civilian authorities had to be taken away, their power, and the weapons had to be taken away from them and put under somebody else's control.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Under whose control?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: They had to be moved to the barracks of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. Mr. Redzic, did the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica accept this decision?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was your personal opinion on that decision?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Already at that time on 1989, I was against that. Not because I had some plans or because I had a premonition. The only reason was the fact that the -- all this had been purchased by the people and I was opposed to somebody taking it away from them. I wanted the materiel and the equipment and the weapons to be used by the people to safeguard the peace and their vital facilities and everything that was envisaged by the law. That's why I was opposed to that. I was the only one at that session, although it has been proven after so many years that I was right at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take the floor? Did you say this?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did take the floor and I said precisely what I'm saying to you today.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, did you have any reason to fear anything at the time? Why did you speak like that?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Of course. The first stage was placing the weapons in the barracks, and I knew that already at that time 90 per cent of the commanders in the army were Serbs, that there was a very small number of Muslims and Catholics, and the few Muslims and Catholics that were there were under the influence of the majority Serbian personnel in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did this mean actually that the weapons were being totally taken away from some peoples in favour of other people?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was clear. It was clear that everybody had to be disarmed and that these weapons would subsequently be distributed amongst another people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What people was that?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the territories of Vlasenica, Bratunac, Zvornik, and Srebrenica, was this decision implemented to the full? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was implemented to the full, not only in this region but in the entire Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically in this region were there any incidents when this weaponry was being taken away from the Territorial Defence and given to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No, there were no incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, according to your information, what happened to those weapons?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: During the first stage, the weapons were placed in the barracks. And then when the conflicts in Slovenia and Croatia broke out, these weapons were already moved to the Serbian territory.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "moved to the Serbian territory," what do you mean by that exactly?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Those same weapons that had been taken away from the Territorial Defence had already been distributed amongst the Serbian population in the municipalities in the subregion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever personally see this distribution of weapons?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion, as I was travelling from Tuzla to Sekovic, I saw a military truck in the centre of the town and I saw the weapons being distributed selectively. I even saw that there were so many young people. I suppose they were students, and they distributed automatic weapons, machine-guns, and similar weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At one moment when you were testifying, you said "selectively," and then you explained that weapons was distributed amongst everybody. Was there a slip of the tongue?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I meant non-selectively, randomly. Everybody was issued with weapons, the elderly, the young, everybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you explain to the Trial Chamber whether Sekovici was a predominantly Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: When I was talking about the national make-up, I already mentioned that Sekovici was almost 100 per cent Serb municipality, and the inner town of Sekovici is 100 per cent Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that they were distributing arms. In your CV we read that you are very well versed in weapons. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice at that time what types of weapons were distributed amongst those people?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Automatic rifles and semi-automatic rifles and machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Redzic. Now I'm going to move on to another topic. Is it true that the multi-party elections were held after these events that concerned the taking away of weapons from the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was on the 18th of November, 1991, that the multi-party elections were taking place. So the things that I have just spoken about had already been completed, all the weapons had already been transferred from the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber very briefly what the results of the municipal -- of the multi-party elections were in the municipalities of Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: As far as the five municipalities are concerned, the SDA won in Zvornik, Bratunac, and Srebrenica, and the SDS in Sekovici and Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also told us that in Vlasenica there was a predominant number of Muslims; however, the Serbian Democratic Party won the elections. What is your opinion of that? How come the SDS won the elections in that municipality? Again, can you please leave some time for the translation.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The post-election analysis showed that the SDS won in Vlasenica because the vast number of Muslims voted for opposition parties, and the opposition parties proposed deputies from the Serb population. That -- Bosniaks gave their votes to the Serbian MPs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what your role was in those elections?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I was the main candidate of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For which municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: For the municipality of Vlasenica. When the elections were over, I was appointed the president of the Executive Board of the Municipal Assembly of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: After these multi-party elections, were leaderships set up in -- at all levels and did they also comprise members of the SDA according to the results of the elections?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the authorities were set up across Bosnia-Herzegovina according to the results of the elections. That is the practice everywhere in the world.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the members of these authorities from the ranks of the SDA hold their own meetings after that?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Of course the SDA was coordinated at the municipal, regional, and state levels, and yes there were regular meetings; this was a novelty in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the goal of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The goal of these meetings of the party and state institutions was to learn the complete information from the area inhabited by the Muslim and Serbian population. It was mostly those two ethnic groups that resided in those areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I am now going to focus on the local level at which these meetings were held. Is it true that at these meetings you received different information from the entire territory of the municipality, for example, the municipality of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. All the Muslim villages were covered by members of the SDA and their role and task as individuals was to inform us of the problems from their respective areas. And then we would be informed about these problems and we really were abreast of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: At these meetings, did you also receive information as to what was going on in the Serbian villages during that period of time, if anything was happening at all?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Those members that were active in the territory, they also monitored the situation in the neighbouring villages and they had to inform us without taking any prior measures. Their role was to come to the municipality and to inform us in detail as to what was going on in the Serbian villages, what certain Serbs were doing, and so on and so forth. So we had a very good insight into the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did these local meetings in the period from 1990 until the beginning of the war, did they happen frequently?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. They would take place every 10 or 15 days or even more often than that, if the situation so required. Sometimes we would meet very often.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you well? Did you say that you also had such meetings at the level of what you call the subregion, at the regional level that is?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have said that and that is the case. We met at the regional level but there are also meetings at the state level. Those meetings were held and it was only logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just for a moment, let's dwell upon these meetings at the regional level. Who were the attendants of those regional meetings of the SDA and the representatives of the municipalities from the Muslim ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was mostly representatives of the SDA and people from the authorities who had been proposed by the SDA. In other words, presidents of the SDA of all municipalities as well as the high officials of all the aforementioned municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there also representatives of Srebrenica and Bratunac present at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, Srebrenica, Bratunac, Zvornik, Sekovici, Vlasenica, and sometimes even the neighbouring municipalities such as Kalesija, Kladanj, Han Pijesak, and Rogatica. It all depended on the situation that prevailed and on many occasions we would also call representatives from the neighbouring municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you attend those meetings as well?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, absolutely, always.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Those regional meetings, how often were they held?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It depended on the situation. They took place every 10 to 15 days, but if the situation so demanded, then we would meet even more often, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, could you please tell the Trial Chamber what you discussed at those meetings, at the regional meetings, that is?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The regional meetings were almost identical to the other meetings; however, we discussed other issues. For example, we presented problems from the municipalities we represented, what was going on, what certain individuals were doing in those municipalities, what certain ethnic groups were doing in those municipalities. In Vlasenica I had complete information as to what was going on as if I myself resided in Sekovici, Srebrenica, and Zvornik, and people from those municipalities were abreast of all the developments in the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since we are talking about the period from 1991 and 1992, did you have any reason to be meeting often because of the situation at the time?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Of course. There were already wars with Slovenia and Croatia. The situation in Bosnia was boiling. The situation on the ground was alarming, and the nature of the events in the territory demanded that we met not only every 10 or 15 days; we were in a constant meeting, so to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. speak. And we didn't -- we had to discuss those topical issues rather than to discuss the economy or similar matters. We were forced by the situation in all the municipalities and in the subregion. I'm talking about the subregion, but the whole of the republic was in a very bad situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also attend some meetings at the republican level, the meetings of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I just said that these meetings were held at the level of the republic and those also took place every fortnight or so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who was it who attended those meetings at the republican level?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Again, there were representatives of the municipal party boards, municipality officials, and many republican officials from the SDA and from some other opposition parties. They would participate in those meetings very often; they would discuss the issues and the ways how to overcome all those problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What specifically did you discuss at those meetings? Was there any two-way communication going on at those meetings?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. We received information from the municipalities all over Bosnia and Herzegovina. The representatives of those municipalities came and talked about the problems there, and in return the republican leadership informed us about their views and the information that they had.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What information did you receive from them? What information did they have?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: As far as the state level is concerned, they received information from various state institutions, the state security, from the Muslims and Croat Catholics that worked there at the time. And they were at the very source of the information on the key issues, much more than we were at the local level on the periphery. If you want to know what they informed us about, they were at the source of the information and they told us that the SDS had created a parastate with the corresponding institutions that they had their Assembly, that they had their Serbian municipalities, their Serbian autonomous regions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, at these meetings did you also discuss military movements, the military situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. There were such discussions, but you could also see all that on television. They did not hesitate to show their movements on television. The top leadership of the republic was duty-bound to inform us of these matters under the constitution.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you at the local level, what kind of information did you provide to the republican organs of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: As for myself and the Vlasenica municipality, I constantly told them that the situation was chaotic, especially further afield in the Vlasenica town. Things were reaching boiling point, and the boundaries of tolerance and understanding were being overstepped.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you speak of the specific situation on the ground? Could the population move about normally?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I told them what the situation was like. In Vlasenica, one didn't know what to do anymore. There were already blockades, Serbs were firing from houses using automatic weapons. The worst kinds of methods of intimidation were used. They called the people "Turks," said they would kill them all. I'm not saying that all the Serbs did that, but those who were responsible did not take any measures. When we, the leadership, discussed that, the SDS leaders did not take any steps. In Vlasenica, long before the war broke out, roads were blocked and people were unable to take timber from the woods.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that. Let me ask you something else now. I will avoid questions dealing with political preparations for the war because the Chamber has heard a lot of evidence about that so far. I will only ask you whether or not it is true that the Serbian Democratic Party in the course of 1991 until the outbreak of the war completed the organising of parallel government bodies?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was already an Assembly of the Serbian People, there were Serb municipalities, and Serb autonomous regions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In view of the fact that you mentioned the Serbian autonomous regions, I won't ask you a lot about the way they were established but I will ask you one question: Which of these Serb autonomous regions that you said were formed in the course of 1991 was highly significant for the developments in Podrinje as of 1991, if so?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: They all had serious repercussions, but as for this area, of course the most serious repercussions and the most painful development was the establishment of the Birac Autonomous Region, which as far as I can recall was established in Sekovici on the 9th of January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if possible could we take a break now because of certain technical problems. I wish to show a short video which is very important to us; however, we were unable to sort this out with the technical staff because the picture and the sound do not match. So we wish to take a short break now in order to sort out this problem if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Certainly, Madam Vidovic. Are you referring to D696?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I have my copy here in case it may help, because sometimes it's the copying that is faulty. So I'm leaving it here just in case you need it. I haven't tried it, so I, myself, don't know if it's -- if the sound and the video is coordinated. But anyway, you have it here. How much time do you require? 30 minutes? We take 25 minutes straight away?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think 30 minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll take 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Have you solved the technical problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Wait. Now, usher, I would like you to go next to the accused to make sure that his monitor is set on the right mode and that he will be able to follow. All right. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please now play the video that's Defence exhibit 696, and it relates to the establishment of the autonomous region, the Serbian Autonomous Region of Birac. The source is the television of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Sarajevo, journalist Salih Brkic. Could you please play the video. It's about two minutes long.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Where is B and H going and on whose way is it? "With the appointment of Milorad Vukanovic from Sekovici as the Assembly Chairman, and Milenko Stanic from Vlasenica as the prime minister designate of the regional government and then by sending a proclamation to the Serb people of Birac, an inaugural session of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Birac was finished today. As they said when making the decision, respecting the right of free choice of every nation, this region is also an expression of desire of the Serb people to live together, in a single state. This is why Birac is proclaimed as an inseparable part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and as a constituent [as interpreted] part of a Federal Unit, Bosnia-Herzegovina. The territory of the Autonomous Region of Birac consisted of Sekovici and Vlasenica municipalities, this decision reads further, and parts of Bratunac, Srebrenica, Zvornik, Kalesija, Kladanj, and Zivinice municipalities. According to the inaugural decision, the region is also open to villages [as interpreted] in the surrounding areas that subsequently decide to join them. As they emphasised upon adoption of this decision, the future Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which would unify the already established areas and regions, shall be the best guarantee for the Serb people in Bosnia and Herzegovina and enable them to join the ... state later. At the same time, a question could be heard during the discussion whether they had considered [as interpreted] economic motives as well, apart from political ones, and concerns were expressed as to whether they had prepared the best possible measures for economic division of the joint 'cake' in the area of Birac. The message, which was conveyed from this gathering to the Serb people of Birac, among other things read: 'Nobody in Sarajevo, Zagreb, and especially Berlin can decide our destiny because never, under no conditions, a single law of the 'Independent Bosnia and Herzegovina,' can reach any Serb house or yard. The request to the European Community to recognise the independent country is a big and significant mistake and there is no return because Bosnia and Herzegovina will share the fate of Yugoslavia,' the message that was conveyed from today's founding Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Birac reads."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, just a while ago you said that you were familiar with this event, that is the establishment of the Birac Serbian Autonomous Region and you told us when it had been established. Could you please explain to the Chamber how the people of Podrinje reacted and can you comment on this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, you can see it all here in this brief report. I don't know whether there's anything we need to add or take away. It was an undercover secession. The Muslim people in this area were truly desperate. They put forward their positions. We heard that only Belgrade and not Zagreb, Sarajevo, or Berlin would discuss their fate. And as far as the Muslim people are concerned, that was practically when war was declared.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Redzic. Did you recognise the people in this report?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I know a good part of the people. For example, Goran Zekic the president of Srebrenica SDS, and also the republican deputy of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there is also Milenko Stanic, a gentleman who was the president of the Vlasenica Municipal Assembly. At this gathering he was elected the prime minister designate. Then there is Jovan Nikolic from Kravica. He was also a highly positioned member of the SDS. There is Milorad Lukic, the president of the Vlasenica SDS. Bozo Milic, who after I was expelled took over the position of the president of the Executive Board of the Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Redzic. Could you please now play the tape further and stop at 015.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Where is Bosnia and Herzegovina going, and in whose way is it? With the appointment of Milorad Okanovic from Sekovici as the assembly chairman and Milenko Stanic from Vlasenica as the prime minister designate of the regional government --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is repeating, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a very small segment in order to identify three persons, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- that we will proceed to talk about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, can you tell the Chamber who this person is?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Milenko Stanic, who as I said was the president of Vlasenica municipality and he was elected at this gathering, the prime minister designate of the Serbian Autonomous Region.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So Milenko Stanic was therefore your president and he was a Serb?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was the president of the Vlasenica Municipal Assembly. He was a Serb by ethnicity. He was a Serb but he was representing all three peoples.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can you continue playing and stop at 024.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Today in Sekovici the constituent session Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Birac was finished today. As they said when making the decision" --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, do you know any of the persons here?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, Jovan Nikolic to the far right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Chamber who Jovan Nikolic is?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: This was a highly ranking member of the SDS and he hails from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you please proceed with the tape and stop at 109, and that will be the last segment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "In adopting this decision it was pointed out that the future" --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, who is this person? Do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: This is Goran Zekic. I've already said that he was the president of the SDS for Srebrenica municipality and also a deputy in the parliament of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Redzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And a note for the interpreters in connection with this video and the following video to be played, we have given the OTP and the Chamber transcripts, and they need not interpret again unless the Chamber wants them to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, I will continue with my questions. Did you have any information about the reactions to these events in the Podrinje area? Did the Muslim people there experience this as secession?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that this video was broadcast by Sarajevo television, the entire population, especially in the Vlasenica municipality, was in a state of chaos. Many people from far afield came to the municipality to complain. They asked what this was all about, whether there was a war on. I attempted to calm people down, to dissuade them from fleeing. People from the borderline areas of the municipalities started coming to the town and to Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please slow down a little for the interpreters. Mr. Redzic, I will now move on to another topic. I won't ask you, as I've already said, about the breakup of Yugoslavia, but I will ask you this: Did you personally observe the arrival of any kind of military forces from outside Bosnia and Herzegovina into Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was evident to all of us in Bosnia and Herzegovina that this was happening, and the television showed this, especially after the conflicts broke out first in Slovenia and then in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell Their Honours when this happened?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: This was in the second half of 1991. In the second half of 1991 there was a large-scale transfer of weapons, equipment, and materiel as well as troops from the neighbouring republics.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now show the witness Defence Exhibit D532.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, this is a document from the federal secretariat for national defence signed by General Veljko Kadijevic from January 1991, and the title is "transfer of forces and equipment from the territory of the Republic of Slovenia order." Please look at paragraph 1. I will quote part of it which says: "Transfer the commands, units, and assets of the JNA from the territory of Slovenia to the territory of the republic," and if you go on it says: "Re-location to Prijedor, Derventa, and Zenica." Are you personally aware of any such re-location of commands, units, installations, and all movable assets to the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina? You said a while ago that you had seen this on television. Were there any cases when some of these units arrived in the Podrinje area? First of all, can you confirm that something like this happened, something like what is described in this document?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I mentioned, the television showed these troop movements and any citizen could see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did some of the JNA units arrive in the Podrinje area, and when?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It's correct that in the second half of 1991, large forces arrived in the area of Zvornik municipality in the Karakaj location. There was a concentration there because during the re-location all kinds of infantry and weapons arrived and were located in Karakaj in the second half of 1991. As for Zvornik municipality -- and as for Vlasenica municipality, in late July a motorised brigade was re-located from Jastrebarsko near Zagreb to the territory of Vlasenica and Sekovici municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, sir, we'll come to that. But let us go back to the units from Zvornik. From whom did you receive this information? How do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: We received this information, as I previously stated, because we had constant meetings, the presidents of municipalities, Executive Boards, and the political parties in all the five municipalities. And at these meetings, the purpose was for everybody to report on any changes in the situation in the area. And the president of the Assembly of Zvornik municipality, Mr. Abdulah Pasic, informed us of the arrival of these units in his municipality, that is in the Karakaj location.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a brigade from Jastrebarsko. Was this an armoured or a mechanised brigade? Did you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I think it was a combined armoured and mechanised brigade which arrived in the area of Vlasenica from Jastrebarsko, near Zagreb. It was re-located to the area of two municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Jastrebarsko is?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Jastrebarsko is close to Zagreb in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher now please show the witness Defence Exhibit 398.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime can anyone tell us the date of that TV broadcast that we saw on D696, please? It's easy to identify because we're talking about the creation of SAO Birac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Your Honour. The way I understood the witness, he mentioned the 9th January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Am I right?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the videotape?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: 9 January, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, kindly look at this exhibit, the one that you have already seen, and can you pay attention to the first paragraph. This document was issued by the police station of Zvornik. The date is 13 October 1991. I'm going to read the first paragraph to you. It says: "We inform you that today, 13 October 1991, at about 8.00 in the morning, a column of military and civilian vehicles was reported transporting reservists on the Tuzla-Zvornik-Loznica road. And while passing through the settlements of Grbavica and Karakaj, and especially as it crossed the bridge in Karakaj, it opened fire (single shots and bursts of automatic gun fire from infantry weapons). The firing continued for a long time throughout the movement of the column in the direction of Loznica. Some vehicles were seen to be moving in the Karakaj-Cepak direction, i.e., from the left bank of the Drina with reservists opening fire on the way. This caused a lot of concern among the inhabitants of the settlements of Grbavci, Zvornik, Karakaj, Celopek, Kozluk, Tasic, Locavic [phoen] et cetera. As a result, the inhabitants themselves came to the SJB in order to report the matter, even telephoning to state that the shooting had frightened many people. Measures of full-scale surveillance of the area by police patrols were taken immediately in order to cooperate with the inhabitants and provide the necessary assistance." Mr. Redzic, you told us that you were aware of the fact that in Karakaj there were military forces. Are you also aware of the fact that these events caused reactions amongst the Muslim population? What kind of reactions were those? Could you describe them for us. What was the feeling that this inspired amongst the Muslim population, if you know?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is a piece of information from one municipality, but similar cases or even worse cases happened elsewhere. However, the fear and anxiety amongst the population of these municipalities that I'm talking about, these existed even before this date here. In other words, the people were frightened. They were anguished. The columns of vehicles passing through the area carried the troops with the insignia that did not correspond to the insignia of the JNA. They sported beards, they lifted three fingers in the air, and they fired through the Muslim villages. And what else could it be but intimidation or, in other words, announcing to the non-Serbian people that they are to -- that they were to fear the worst.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is Karakaj a Serbian village? In other words, the area where these troops were billeted in Zvornik, is this predominantly Serb?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, by and large. The army always avoided such locations where at least one part of the population was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now look at another map for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to show the witness another map. We have copied the map to enable the Chamber and the learned friends from the Prosecution to follow what is being said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, look at the map. I will take you back to the 2nd Brigade which moved from Jastrebarsko to the Podrinje area, where you resided. Could you please explain to us, if you can, where the 2nd Brigade was billeted. Let me just explain before you answer the question. The map that we have distributed is a map of the military geographic institute. It is a topographic map of the Kladanj-Zvornik region. The scale is 1:100.000. It shows the Vlasenica/Srebrenica area. You can see the town of Srebrenica itself. Can you please show to the Trial Chamber where Vlasenica is and can you please encircle Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've encircled it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you please tell us now, do you have any information about where this brigade from Jastrebarsko was billeted?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: As I've already told you some troops were in Lukic Polje, in Vlasenica municipality, and the other troops in Tisca in the Sekovici municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show that on the map where is Tisca. Could you look at the crossroads?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, thank you, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they show very well. And can you also show Lukic Polje?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have encircled Lukic Polje as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you please tell us whether these were Serbian or Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: This was a 100 per cent Serb-populated area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, did you perceive the presence of these units yourself, did you see them yourself on the ground?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: As I was moving in different directions towards Tuzla, Bratunac, and Srebrenica, and as I was inspecting the areas of Vlasenica and other areas, I convinced myself that there were very strong forces with tanks, Howitzers, Pragas, and other artillery tools deployed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally see the movements of these units?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. They would move during the day. They would march, and this was done to intimidate people from Vlasenica towards Mijoci [phoen]. Another group would go from Bratunac to the Drina River. And the third marching group was from Tisca, Vlasenica to Han Pijesak. They would descend to military and then they would go towards Srebrenica and then on the old road towards the bauxite mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you saw these tanks and transporters moving, when was that?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was in the second half of 1991. During that period of time, as soon as they arrived, maybe 15 minutes later after having been deployed in their positions, they constantly moved around and I also received information from the ground about those movements, about everything that the column did, that they were shooting through the Muslim-settled areas, that there were soldiers with the special insignia, that they lifted three fingers in the air, and they did everything that irritated the people and that served to provoke Muslims into a bloodshed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the same map, could you please show the Trial Chamber where Han Pijesak is.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I can see that you have done that, that you've encircled Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber how far is Han Pijesak from Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: The distance between Han Pijesak and Vlasenica is 18 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How far is it from Srebrenica by road and how far it is as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: 50 kilometres by road and as the crow flies between 15 and 20 kilometres, whereas Vlasenica is only about 5 kilometres away as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, could you tell the Trial Chamber what is the significance of Han Pijesak as a military stronghold. What was its significance before the war, that is, if you know?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Before the war, Han Pijesak had barracks with some 1500 troops and all the accompanying equipment that is necessary for a military. In the vicinity of Han Pijesak, there was a depot, a military depot called Zepa. That's where the most modern equipment was and everything that was necessary. This depot in the former Yugoslavia was planned as an atomic shelter for the supreme command of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: How did you learn about that? How did you get by this information? How come you know that? How come you know this about Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I heard that information earlier. I went to Han Pijesak very often with the commander of the barracks in Han Pijesak, Mr. Milosevic. I spoke to him about many things.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you talk about?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: We spoke about all sorts of things. We started talking in 1990 at the moment when there is the conflict in Croatia and Slovenia, when the situation became tense in Bosnia, when the worst was feared. My position was, bearing in mind that they were in our vicinity, I considered that the Yugoslav People's Army, as the army of all the peoples, I would go there very often to talk to Mr. Milosevic, who would later on become the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. I wanted to carry out mobilisation of the Territorial Defence in Vlasenica municipality in order to protect the vital interests of these areas and thus ensure the safety of all the citizens.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did he accept your proposals?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: On several occasions, I made proposals to him, but he openly said to me that he would not give one single rifle to a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this map into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this will become Defence Exhibit D706. I think it's the case, as is being pointed to us, that the witness initials the map before we accept it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please put your initials on the map.

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, you have described for us the arrival of this brigade and the situation that ensued after the arrival of that brigade and how the Muslim population felt on that account in the second half of 1991. The Muslim population of the area, could they move freely throughout the entire municipality?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: No. In 1991 in Vlasenica municipality, there were all sorts of incidents and inappropriate behaviour on the part of some Serbs and their reservists. There was a lot of provocation and taunting of students in the buses. The workers who came from the neighbouring villages to Vlasenica to work, they were also taunted and provoked. As I've already said, the army provoked people. They displayed irritating behaviour and there were even bans on carrying out certain work. For example, there was a ban on felling.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, just for a moment could we dwell upon what you have just mentioned. You have mentioned the ban issued to the workers of the forestry company of Birac to do the felling in the woods. Can you explain the information that you had. Why did this happen? Did you ever learn the reasons behind the ban on the exploitation of timber in the area?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was my duty as the president of the municipality to look after the security and safety situation in my municipality. The director of the forestry company called us, his name was Ibran Nuhanovic. He asked us to try and solve the problem. I asked him to call the town hall meeting. He did that. He invited me and M. Stanic to attend that meeting. At the meeting you could hear that the workers were banned from working in the forest because the Serbs had already deployed their artillery there, their Howitzers, mortars, and the accompanying material and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the exploitation of the assets. What did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I had in mind timber and felling.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, is it true that Mr. Stanic, the Serbian president of the municipality from the ranks of the Serbian people attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was -- there were a number of Serbs who were opposed to such bans because their families relied on that work. And if they didn't work, it was only logical that they would not be paid and that they would not be able to provide for their families.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you send a report on this event? And if you did, who did you send it to?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: I sent my reports to the republican bodies. I informed the Presidency, the government, and the competent ministries. In this particular case, I reported to the minister for forestry.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also mentioned meetings of municipal officials at the local level. Did you have similar information based on their information, if they provided it to you, from the municipalities of Srebrenica and Bratunac about similar events, the events of that sort?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. The same thing that I had in my municipality and the problems that I faced there, the gentlemen that attended those meetings informed us about the problems in the municipalities of Bratunac, Srebrenica, Zvornik, and even Sekovici to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When it comes to the municipality of Srebrenica, who was it who submitted the reports of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was Mr. Ibran Mustafic and the president of the Municipal Assembly -- what was his name? It was in any case the president of the Municipal Assembly, and Mr. Ibran Mustafic, he was the president of the Executive Board and I spoke to him more often.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When it comes to Bratunac, you remember who was the rapporteur from Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was mostly the president of the municipality, Mr. Nijaz Dubicic. He was the one who spoke about the problems and situation in the territory of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of information did they provide you with about the events in their territories in the second half of 1991 until the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: IZET REDZIC
utterances.text: It was an unwritten rule. The situation was the same, the problems were the same. They provided us with information from the area inhabited by the Serbs. They said they had huge problems, that people are being armed, that they gathered into groups, that they were being provided with weapons, not even illegally anymore, but openly and publicly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can the witness be shown Defence exhibit D690, page 176, please -- actually, the last -- could you please show the witness page 175 and 176. Your Honour, in the English version you will find this on page 24 -- 24, the part that I'm going to show to the witness. This is on page 24 of the English translation of the document --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't speak English, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to avoid wasting time, I have the document before me. I can assist you with the copy that I have. Could you please show the witness the first sentence -- actually, the last sentence on page 175, and the first paragraph on page 176, the paragraph is in bold script.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the last sentence on page 175, and I'm going to read it to you --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but if we could have a moment. I'm actually trying to locate this English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She said page 224 -- no, page 24. No, no, no, it's page 24. In the English text that I have there is only a page 24 --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, page 24, bottom-right corner is the page that you ...

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I want to make sure that they have the --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, it's just that -- I don't doubt that it's here. It's just the way that it was -- it's somewhat in excerpts and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. You may have a completely different -- we're talking of ERN 01102509, that's the page that I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we'll locate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If my learned friend could look at me, maybe you will be able to find it if I show this bolded part of the text. Maybe I can assist you with that. It is the last paragraph on page 24 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We're talking --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We're talking of Friday, 3rd April, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHARDSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Friday, 3rd April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
